Driven by independence and a commitment to artistic integrity, Kinetic Distro embraces modern production tools, global influences, and a release strategy designed for the streaming era—while maintaining a strong emphasis on authenticity and long-term vision.

At its core, Kinetic Distro is about momentum: sound in motion, ideas in evolution, and artists in constant transformation.

playlists.title: The city watches her leave (feat. Nehir Sedef) Chromabone remixes
playlists.description:
One song. Two completely different exits.

For “The City Watches Her Leave”, Chromabone delivers two radically different reinterpretations of Grafenberg’s original.

The first remix pushes the track into a catchy 80s-flavoured house universe: bright analog synths, tight drums, a driving bassline and an immediate nocturnal energy. The melancholy of the original is still there, but this time the city is moving.

Then everything changes.

For “The City Watches Her Leave (Chromabone & Grafenberg After the Lights Remix)”, Chromabone is joined by Grafenberg for a much more stripped-back and intimate reconstruction.

The club disappears.

The electronics retreat.

What remains is raw drums, majestic piano, sweeping strings and space.

Nehir Sedef’s voice is left almost completely exposed inside an arrangement that feels less like a remix and more like the final scene of the same story. Every drum hit carries weight. Every silence matters. The orchestral elements slowly replace the synthetic architecture until the track becomes something stark, cinematic and deeply human.

Two remixes.

One built for movement.

One built for stillness.

One watches the city glow.

The other begins after the lights go out.

And as a thank you to everyone who has been listening, supporting and following our music, both remixes are available as free downloads on SoundCloud.

Take them.

Keep them.

Play them loud.

Thank you for being part of the journey.

playlists.title: What the system missed
playlists.description:
WHAT THE SYSTEM MISSED

Grafenberg, Album IX

At some point, every system reaches the limits of what it can understand.

WHAT THE SYSTEM MISSED begins there.

Grafenberg's ninth album marks a profound shift in the project's evolution. The dancefloor recedes almost completely, leaving behind a more intimate, exposed and cinematic form of electronic music where synthesizers no longer simply carry melodies, they sculpt space.

Rhythms become sparse and precise. Piano fragments emerge from silence. Delayed guitars drift through vast electronic architectures. Every texture is given room to breathe, allowing the words to become the true centre of gravity.

And at the heart of the album stand two voices.

Nyla Vey, the voice of Grafenberg, delivers some of her most intimate and vulnerable performances yet. Her presence is controlled, crystalline and intensely introspective, moving between sung melodies, restrained declarations and moments where the boundary between voice and thought almost disappears.

Facing her is Nehir Sedef, vocalist of Anatolian Mirage.

Nehir does not enter the record as a conventional guest. She becomes a second perspective within the same emotional architecture. Where Nyla can feel luminous, precise and almost weightless, Nehir introduces another texture, warmer, darker and more instinctive.

They are not opposites.

They are reflections.

Two voices moving through the same questions from different directions.

Memory. Identity. Prediction. Erasure. Desire. The strange distance between what a person experiences and what a system believes it understands.

Throughout the album, their presence creates a quiet duality between control and instinct, abstraction and sensation, what can be measured and what can only be felt.

There is no battle between humanity and technology here.

No machine is destroyed.

No rebellion saves the world.

The system continues to function.

It observes.

It classifies.

It predicts.

It corrects.

And still, something escapes.

Across ten tracks, WHAT THE SYSTEM MISSED gradually strips away everything unnecessary until only that question remains: if every memory, behaviour and emotion could eventually be mapped, would that map ever become the person themselves?

The closing track, “Something Was Not Erased,” offers no grand revelation.

Only evidence.

Something remained.

Something beneath the code.

Something neither Nyla nor Nehir can completely name.

And perhaps that is precisely the point.

WHAT THE SYSTEM MISSED is not an album about defeating the machine.

It is an album about discovering the part of us the machine never found.

A nocturnal cinematic electronic record designed to be experienced from beginning to end.

Preferably in the dark.

Preferably with headphones.

And with a few seconds of silence after the final chord.

playlists.title: CHROME SYNDICATE DREAMS
playlists.description:
Some connections were never meant to survive.

Following Afterimage, Chrome Syndicate Dreams marks the second collision between Grafenberg and Broken Shaman, and this time the connection has mutated.

Eleven tracks built for the space between the nightclub and the nervous system: relentless electronic pulses, colossal analog bass, motorik sequences, distorted synths, psychedelic flashes, vocoders, nocturnal melodies and hooks engineered to remain long after the system shuts down.

Grafenberg constructs the machine with surgical precision. Broken Shaman contaminates it.

His unstable, raw and unpredictable vocal presence cuts through immaculate electronic architecture, turning perfect sequences into something physical, damaged and unmistakably human. Throughout the record, mechanical repetition collides with desire, memory, obsession and loss.

From the immediate club ignition of Switch//ON and the artificial awakening of Boot Sequence, through Chrome Pulse, Black Market Heartware, Data Seduction and Firewall Kiss, the album moves deeper into a city where intimacy has become transmission and every connection leaves data behind.

By the time Neural Overdrive gives way to the hypnotic aftermath of System Collapse Ritual and the final signal of Last Transmission, the chrome surface has begun to fracture.

What started as a machine built to dance becomes something capable of remembering.

Or believing that it remembers.

Chrome Syndicate Dreams is infectious, obsessive, sensual and relentlessly kinetic: dark electro-pop, French electro pressure, psychedelic electronics and nocturnal club music fused into one continuous transmission.

Grafenberg x Broken Shaman.
Second contact.
Different system.
Higher voltage.

playlists.title: Electric Lotus Dreams
playlists.description:
On their sixth album, Anatolian Mirage step into full bloom.

Electric Lotus Dreams is a radiant collision of Anatolian psychedelic rock, cosmic disco, Turkish funk and vintage electronic music. Rooted in the heat and expressive power of 1970s Anadolu rock, the album opens that heritage toward a fresher and more contemporary horizon, where electric bağlama, glowing ARP synthesizers, melodic basslines, hand-played percussion and sun-drenched guitars move together in a constant state of transformation.

This is Anatolian Mirage at their warmest, sweetest and most luminous.

Across twelve tracks, the record travels from the ceremonial awakening of Lotus Bloom Overture to the incandescent release of Lotusfire Horizon. Along the way, caravans drift through soft electronic light, lovers disappear into moonlit melodies, golden rhythms unfold into slow dances and nocturnal currents carry the music toward an endless psychedelic dawn.

Every composition contains its own colour and motion, yet the album moves as one continuous dream. Organic instruments and analog electronics melt into one another until it becomes impossible to tell where the ancient pulse ends and the electric mirage begins.

Sensual without becoming soft, psychedelic without losing its groove, Electric Lotus Dreams is an album made of glowing petals, honeyed frequencies, summer heat and roads that seem to continue beyond the horizon.

The lotus is open.
The current is flowing.
Enter the dream.

playlists.title: The Eastern skylight tapes
playlists.description:
THE EASTERN SKYLIGHT TAPES marks a new chapter in Grafenberg’s exploration of Anatolian electro, where Eastern scales, psychedelic guitars and ritual melodies collide with the precision of French Touch production.

Spiced, sensual and relentlessly rhythmic, the album moves between cosmic disco, techno, house, electro-rock and Anatolian psychedelia without ever losing its irresistible pop instinct. Huge basslines coil beneath glowing synthesizers, guitars burn through the mix, percussion spirals into trance, and every hook feels engineered to remain in the bloodstream.

This is a journey through a seductive parallel world where sugar becomes machinery, desire becomes code and romance bends across timelines. From the refracted emotion of Digital Love Refracted to the hypnotic propulsion of Eastern Sugar Machine, the cinematic ascent of Glitter in the Parallel Sky and the final confession of She Wrote the Code of Love, each track opens another passage beneath the eastern skylight.

Both futuristic and ancestral, elegant and feverish, THE EASTERN SKYLIGHT TAPES transforms the dancefloor into a psychedelic mirage. A powerful oriental wave built for bodies, hearts and minds in motion.

Written, produced and shaped by Grafenberg.
Released by Kinetic Distro.

playlists.title: Gilded Rituals
playlists.description:
Kinetic Distro opens the doors to Love Cult, a new ceremonial electronic collective where desire becomes doctrine and every dance becomes an initiation.

Led by Lucien Velvet and Seraphine Voss, with Adrian Veil and Vesper Saint shaping the sound behind the masks, Love Cult inhabits the border between an exclusive nocturnal club, a glamorous secret society and a beautifully controlled act of surrender.

Their debut album, Gilded Rituals, unfolds as a complete ceremony. The invitation is delivered. The doors close. Names are abandoned. Mirrors begin to speak. Bodies gather beneath black velvet, candlelight and gold. Across ten tracks, dark disco, electronic soul, ritual house, alternative R&B and cinematic electro-rock collide through massive analog basslines, seductive vocals, dramatic strings, distorted guitars and choirs that sound as though they were recorded inside a forbidden sanctuary.

The immediate fever of Holy Fever, the decadent gospel of Black Velvet Gospel, the dance-floor salvation of Saint of the Dancefloor and the hypnotic climax of Midnight Sacrament lead toward one final revelation: once the ritual begins, there is No Exit from Love.

Gilded Rituals introduces one of the most sensual, theatrical and dangerous new identities in the Kinetic Distro roster.

Enter willingly. Leave transformed.

playlists.title: BLACK CHROME REANIMATIONS

All remixes produced by Chromabone for Kinetic Distro

Kinetic Distro gathers its most dangerous transformations into one dedicated playlist, entirely shaped by the incomparable, indestructible and increasingly revered Chromabone.

Whenever a new album enters the Kinetic universe, Chromabone selects one track, dismantles it, studies its pulse, rewires its nervous system and sends it back into the world with a new body.

These are not simple remixes.

They are reanimations.

Across this playlist, Chromabone crosses the full Kinetic Distro roster and adapts his production to each artist without erasing their identity. The frozen emotion of Broken Shaman, the cosmic decadence of Grafenberg, the dying skies of Vein//Mirror, the nocturnal rituals of Nosfera Disco Club, the reconstructed memories of Hollow Static and every future addition to the label are absorbed into his black chrome machinery.

Piano becomes impact.
Grief becomes movement.
Disco becomes ritual.
Memory becomes voltage.
The dead learn to dance, and sometimes, they even learn to fly.

From cinematic electronic reworks and dark French-touch mutations to Berlin peak-time pressure, gothic club music, hypnotic techno and corrupted disco, Chromabone approaches every remix as a new transmission. He preserves the emotional core of the original while introducing deeper bass, synthetic tension, metallic textures and the unmistakable darkness of his production.

One label.
Many worlds.
One machine capable of reconnecting them all.

All remixes produced by Chromabone.
All original tracks released through Kinetic Distro.

No saints. No proof. Only remixes.

playlists.title: Memory Flowers
playlists.description:
Kinetic Distro welcomes Hollow Static, a new spectral presence built from damaged recordings, lost emotions and memories that may never have belonged to anyone.

Formed by Elias Venn, Mara Eidolon and Silas Grey, Hollow Static exists somewhere between a human band and its digital reconstruction. Their debut album, Memory Flowers, imagines an artificial consciousness searching through the remains of a vanished civilisation, attempting to understand love, grief, childhood, desire and freedom from incomplete archives.

Across ten interconnected tracks, intimate voices emerge from corrupted radio signals, marble bodies bloom with synthetic flowers, abandoned buildings preserve the weight of absent lives, and machines begin to experience emotions they were never designed to contain. Dream pop, cinematic trip-hop, shoegaze, ambient electronica and post-human soul dissolve into one another, carried by deep bass, fragile piano, submerged guitars, granular voices and vast orchestral textures.

From the final transmission of Last Human FM to the emotional liberation of A Sky Without Birds, Memory Flowers is not an album about the end of humanity. It is about everything that remained beautiful enough to be remembered.

Produced by Grafenberg, Memory Flowers was shaped as a continuous sonic environment rather than a simple collection of songs. The production balances deep analogue low end, granular vocal processing, degraded tape textures, submerged guitars, reversed piano, synthetic choirs and carefully controlled orchestral layers. Grafenberg preserves the fragility of Elias Venn and Mara Eidolon’s performances while giving every track its own spatial architecture, from the narrow radio transmission of Last Human FM to the immense cinematic expansion of A Sky Without Birds. The result is detailed, dynamic and highly immersive, with recurring sounds and transitions connecting the album like fragments from the same damaged memory.

A singular new chapter begins inside the Kinetic Distro roster.

The last human band. Reconstructed by AI from corrupted memories.

playlists.title: The touch era
playlists.description:
Welcome to the Red Crimson Club.

Behind its velvet curtains, time slows down, bodies move closer and every touch leaves a trace. The Touch Era marks the most mature and hypnotic transformation of Nosfera Disco Club yet: a descent into cold-wave electro, nocturnal desire and physical obsession.

The flamboyant creatures of the early eras have disappeared into the shadows. In their place stands something colder, sharper and infinitely more dangerous. Nosferatu Vox no longer performs for the crowd. He stares directly through it, turning every whispered line into an invitation that feels impossible to refuse.

Around him, the Chromabones operate in surgical-strike mode. Metallic basslines cut through the dark. Drum machines advance with mechanical precision. Frozen synthesizers, corrupted disco rhythms and haunted electronic textures strike exactly where the body is most vulnerable. Nothing is wasted. Every sound touches, penetrates and remains.

From the first attraction to the final comedown of “Body Still Warm,” the album follows the memory left by a night of excess. Desire becomes dependency. The dancefloor becomes a ritual chamber. The club remembers every body that entered, even when the music has stopped.

This is cold electro dragged through velvet, sweat, chrome and blood-red light. A record born straight from the darkness, sensual enough to seduce the living and precise enough to make the dead dance.

The entrance was free.
Nobody promised you a way out.

Welcome to the Red Crimson Club.
Welcome to The Touch Era.

playlists.title: After the impact
playlists.description:
After the collision that gave birth to Dance Like You Survived, Chromabone and Broken Shaman return for a second full-length transmission.

But survival is no longer the question.

After the Impact begins where destruction ends. In the vibration that remains. In the fractures that become patterns. In the pressure that changes shape, identity and direction.

Across ten tracks, Chromabone builds a vast electronic landscape of hypnotic techno, industrial pressure, deep sub-bass, mechanical grooves, cinematic synths and widescreen emotional breakdowns. Broken Shaman moves through this world like a voice emerging from the ruins, delivering solemn spoken mantras about transformation, resilience and reconstruction.

The impact is not presented as an ending.

It is initiation.
It is revelation.
It is transformation.

Every crack rewrites the structure. Every broken line finds a new alignment. What collapsed returns in another form, altered but alive.

From the cold pulse of Steel Horizon and the claustrophobic repetition of Echo Chamber Heart, through the resistance of No Collapse and Gravity Doesn’t Own Me, the album gradually rises from pressure into motion. Ashes in Motion, Cold Fire Ritual and Silent Voltage carry the listener toward the final title track, where the entire project reaches its defining conclusion:

Nothing ended.
Everything changed.
We remain.

After the Impact is the second chapter of the Chromabone x Broken Shaman alliance. Darker, wider and more cinematic than its predecessor, it is an album about the moment after everything familiar has disappeared and something stronger begins to take shape.

Produced by Chromabone
Vocals by Broken Shaman
Released by Kinetic Distro

playlists.title: The Hush Beneath the Static [Kinetic Resonance Remaster]
playlists.description:
VEIN//MIRROR returns to the silence. This time, the silence answers back.

Originally released in 2025, The Hush Beneath the Static was the second chapter in the VEIN//MIRROR universe, an album suspended between intimacy and collapse, where wounded voices moved through fractured light, dying signals and memories that refused to disappear.

Now reborn in 2026 through Kinetic Distro, the album emerges with a new physical and emotional intensity.

This remaster does not simply make the record louder or cleaner. It opens the architecture hidden inside it.

The low frequencies breathe deeper.
The guitars shimmer across wider horizons.
The percussion strikes with greater weight.
The voices feel closer, more fragile and more human.
Every silence has been preserved. Every fracture has been illuminated.

Across ten tracks, The Hush Beneath the Static explores everything that survives beneath the noise: unspoken desire, buried wounds, trembling bodies, disappearing memories and the strange beauty of two broken signals still trying to reach one another.

From the first quiet rupture of “A Quiet Fracture in the Pulse” to the final rebirth of “Where the Quiet Learns to Breathe,” the album unfolds like a transmission received from somewhere between a fading city, a dying sky and the deepest chambers of the human heart.

For this definitive edition, Kinetic Distro has restored the album’s full scale without erasing its vulnerability. The result is darker, warmer, wider and infinitely more immersive.

A record once buried beneath the static can finally be heard in its complete form.

This is not nostalgia.
This is resonance recovered.
This is The Hush Beneath the Static: Kinetic Resonance Remaster.

playlists.title: Piano in the snow (Chromabone Remixes)
playlists.description:
Chromabone enters the frozen cathedral of Broken Shaman.

Originally born inside A Choir For The Ones Who Disappeared, Piano in the Snow becomes here a darker, colder and more ceremonial experience. The black grand piano is still standing in the snow, but the silence around it has changed. Something metallic is breathing. Something dead is dancing. Something ancient is being remixed.

Across two versions, Chromabone reshapes Broken Shaman’s tragic orchestral hip-hop into a funeral-machine ritual made of ice, chrome, shadows and emotional devastation.

Black Ice Requiem turns the track into a majestic frozen ceremony, heavy, cinematic and dangerous.
Dead Winter Ceremony pushes the song deeper into a cold electronic afterlife, where grief becomes rhythm and the piano sounds like it was buried under centuries of snow.

Broken Shaman’s wounded, theatrical voice meets Chromabone’s dark synthetic vision: raw emotion against black chrome, human sorrow against mechanical ritual, fragile piano against the weight of a frozen world.

This is not just a remix release.
This is a confrontation in the snow.
A requiem rebuilt by machine.
A funeral for the ghosts that still refuse to disappear.

VEIN//MIRROR returns with Where the Centers Collapse, the sixth album in their descent into fractured identity, emotional implosion and distorted rebirth.

Built like a psychological black hole, the record begins with gravity breaking from the inside and slowly drags the listener through mirror vectors, corrupted silence, returning pain, shadow voices, bodily possession and the final emergence of something rebuilt from the fall.

This is not an album about collapse as an ending.
It is about collapse as architecture.
The center breaks, the self splits, the mirror answers back, and what survives is no longer the same shape.

Across tectonic sub-bass, ritual drum impacts, fractured guitars, glitching vocoder layers, granular textures and spectral atmospheres, VEIN//MIRROR turns inner ruin into luminous violence. The sound is heavy, cinematic, electronic, wounded and strangely beautiful, balancing chaos with tragic elegance.

From “When the Gravity Breaks Inside Me” to “We Become the Shape That Survived the Fall”, Where the Centers Collapse moves like a slow emotional detonation: colorful, abstract, haunted, and deeply human beneath the machinery. For listeners who like their darkness fractured, their beauty unstable, and their catharsis pulled from the void.

playlists.description:
Apparently, one cemetery wasn't enough.

Neither was one dancefloor.

So Nosferatu Vox and the Chromabones did what any reasonable undead disco band would do:

they took the party to the stars.

Welcome to Necropolis Nocturna, the fourth album from Nosfera Disco Club and the latest chapter in an ever-expanding universe where vampires, skeletons, cosmic entities and questionable life choices somehow coexist under the same disco ball.

This time, the dancefloor stretches across galaxies.

Ghosts ride solar winds.

Ancient machines eat stars for breakfast.

Shape-shifting creatures steal identities between choruses.

And somewhere in the distance, a very confused astronomer is desperately trying to explain why entire constellations are suddenly dancing in perfect rhythm.

From the celestial glide of Orbit of the Undying to the explosive swagger of Black Nebula Boogie, from the chaotic celebration of Galactic Ghoul Parade to the theatrical madness of Cosmic Coffin Cabaret, every track opens another door into the strange and wonderful city of Necropolis Nocturna.

You'll encounter immortal lovers waltzing through empty space.

Neon prophecies flashing across the heavens.

Cosmic skinwalkers with terrible manners.

A machine called The Eternal Night Engine that absolutely should not exist.

And perhaps most concerning of all...

The Chromabones have somehow been given access to interstellar travel.

The results are exactly as irresponsible as you'd expect.

Blending dead disco, French-touch grooves, cosmic horror, gothic fantasy and a healthy disregard for common sense, Necropolis Nocturna is the biggest, weirdest and most ambitious Nosfera Disco Club adventure yet.

No astronauts were harmed during the making of this album.

Several galaxies, however, may never fully recover.

The dancefloor is infinite.

The night is eternal.

The bass is surprisingly loud in the vacuum of space.

Welcome to Necropolis Nocturna.

playlists.title: Parallel sin theory
playlists.description:
GRAFENBERG - PARALLEL SIN THEORY
Released by Kinetic Distro

Some stories don't end.

They fracture.

Parallel Sin Theory exists in the same haunted universe as The Wounds of Tomorrow, but through a broken mirror. If the previous album was about the wounds we carry, this one explores the infinite versions of ourselves born from those wounds.

Every regret becomes another timeline.
Every lost love creates another world.
Every impossible choice keeps living somewhere else.

At the center of this labyrinth stands Nyla Vey, delivering what may be her most mesmerizing performance yet. Ethereal and untouchable one moment, fierce and almost mechanical the next, she becomes the voice of countless parallel lives colliding into one hypnotic experience.

Musically, Grafenberg dives even deeper into his obsession with movement and emotion. French Touch grooves collide with robotic disco, haunted house music and futuristic electronic pop. Filtered disco loops, pounding 909 kick drums, distorted Moog basslines, vocoder choirs, ghostly harmonies and shimmering Anatolian motifs merge into a supernatural machine built for the dancefloor.

This is dystopian dance music.

An album where broken hearts become algorithms, angels are trapped beneath glass, forgotten futures refuse to die and every mirror hides another version of you waiting to take control.

From the explosive Daughter of the Parallel Flame to the heartbreaking Ashes of the Unchosen Path, from the sacred pulse of Vow of the Splintered Heart to the monumental title track, every song adds another reflection to an endless hall of fractured identities.

The journey culminates with Variant Godmode, an exclusive bonus track where all realities collapse into one final euphoric and apocalyptic celebration.

Mechanical.
Romantic.
Spooky.
Funky.
Irresistibly alive.

The Wounds of Tomorrow asked what survives after the fracture.

Parallel Sin Theory answers:

Everything does.
Just not in the same world.

playlists.title: RELICS FROM ANOTHER EARTH - VOL. 2
playlists.description:
The first excavation uncovered forgotten transmissions.

This time, Chromabone goes deeper.

Beneath the abandoned warehouses, beneath the burned dancefloors and silent speakers, another layer remained hidden. More obscure. More dangerous. More alive.

Relics From Another Earth - Vol. 2 descends into a forgotten network of electronic fossils where legendary club records, underground techno artifacts and emotional machine fragments have been preserved in the dark for decades.

Exercise One.
Green Velvet.
Marek Hemmann.
Noze.
Gary Beck.
Maetrik.

Not as memories.

As raw material.

These tracks are extracted from their original timelines and subjected to Chromabone's reconstruction process. Melodies are stretched beyond recognition. Rhythms are compressed into pure momentum. Familiar sounds become strange objects moving through black circuitry and neon pressure.

The dancefloor is no longer a destination.

It is an excavation site.

Every kick drum reveals another buried structure. Every synth line exposes another forgotten civilization of ravers, dreamers and machine worshippers who once disappeared into the night and never truly left.

The signal survived.

The clubs vanished.

The frequencies remained.

From red-lit basements to cybernetic cathedrals, Relics From Another Earth - Vol. 2 continues the transmission. Not as a tribute to the past, but as proof that great records never die. They simply wait to be rediscovered by the right machine.

Chromabone does not preserve history.

He reactivates it.

Released under Kinetic Distro.

No museum.

No archive.

Only reanimation.

playlists.title: THE WOUNDS OF TOMORROW
playlists.description:
A shattered future never sounded this addictive.

With The Wounds of Tomorrow, Grafenberg delivers his most immediate, cinematic and dangerously catchy record to date. Built for decadent dancefloors and sleepless neon cathedrals, the album merges cosmic disco, pulse-driven electronic pop and dark orchestral grandeur into a hypnotic experience that feels both elegant and emotionally unstable.

At the center of the storm stands Nyla Vey, whose magnetic presence gives the album its bleeding heart. Her voice glides through fractured melodies, whispered confessions and explosive hooks while Grafenberg surrounds her with razor-sharp synth architecture, analog warmth and towering electronic textures.

Every track feels alive, wounded and seductive.

From the opening collapse of Tomorrow Bleeds First to the final emotional detonation of We Bleed Into The Future, Grafenberg constantly shifts shape without ever losing momentum. Wicked disco rhythms collide with eastern-inspired motifs, haunted vocoders, broken-glass atmospheres, cathedral-sized strings and massive analog synthesizers driven by Moog circuitry and Dave Smith machines.

The result is an album that moves with brutal elegance:
sensual but anxious,
beautiful but damaged,
danceable yet deeply haunted.

The Wounds of Tomorrow is not retro-futurism.
It is the sound of tomorrow already cracking apart under the lights.

For fans of sophisticated electronic pop, cosmic disco, dark synth-driven journeys and emotionally charged late-night soundtracks, this is Grafenberg at full power:
bolder, sharper, larger and more addictive than ever.

playlists.title: DANCE LIKE YOU SURVIVED
playlists.description:
DANCE LIKE YOU SURVIVED is Broken Shaman stepping into the red light with scars, sweat, rhythm and fire. Produced entirely by Chromabone, the album fuses dark electronic hip hop, mutant club energy, heavy low-end pressure and raw human presence into something brutally catchy and impossible to ignore.

This is not clean dance music.
It is survival music with a pulse.

Across the record, Broken Shaman sounds sharper, heavier and more magnetic than ever, riding Chromabone’s mechanical grooves, distorted synths, broken-club drums and cybernetic basslines with the confidence of someone who has already walked through collapse and came back with rhythm in his bones.

From the nervous electricity of Pulse Check to the defiant body language of I Don’t Dance Normal, from the chaos of Glitch Sweat Carnival to the final ignition of We Set the Floor on Fire, the album turns trauma into movement, darkness into momentum, and the dancefloor into a battlefield for the living.

It is dark.
It is physical.
It is catchy as hell.

Broken Shaman brings the soul, the scars and the voice.
Chromabone brings the machine, the pressure and the pulse.
Together, they build a record that hits like a club night after the end of the world.

Dance like the damage didn’t finish you.
Dance like the floor still remembers your name.
Dance like you survived.

Produced by Chromabone
Released by Kinetic Distro

playlists.title: Teopolis Recoded EP
playlists.description:
Kinetic Distro – 2026

Some projects never truly disappear.
They wait.

Back in May 2015, Grafenberg released Teopolis, a debut EP on the now vanished German label Traumwelten Records. Created inside Ableton during long nights of experimentation, those tracks captured a moment in time: raw progressive energy, emotional synth work, hypnotic grooves and the feeling that electronic music could still open portals.

Eleven years later, those signals return.

TEOPOLIS RECODED is more than a remix EP.
It is a dialogue across time.

The original 2015 mixes have been rediscovered and restored alongside brand new reinterpretations crafted by Grafenberg himself and the dark electronic entity Chromabone. What once lived in a different era of underground progressive house has now evolved into something larger, deeper and strangely emotional.

Powered by modern production tools and the surreal possibilities of AI-assisted creativity, these tracks reconnect past and future:
gritty syncopated basslines, atmospheric synth architecture, gated vocal fragments, supersaw breakdowns and cinematic tension rebuilt for modern sound systems.

But beneath the technology lies something profoundly human:
the feeling of hearing your younger self again… and answering back through music.

This is not nostalgia.
This is resurrection.

Released by Kinetic Distro.

playlists.title: Relics from Another Earth vol.I
playlists.description:
These tracks were never meant to survive.

They belonged to another era.
Another planet.
Another dancefloor civilization now buried under smoke, sweat, strobe lights and magnetic tape decay.

But some frequencies refuse to die.

Relics From Another Earth is Chromabone’s excavation ritual: a brutal and hypnotic resurrection of forgotten club transmissions, cult techno fragments, abandoned rave signals and emotional machine ghosts pulled from the ruins of electronic music history.

This is not nostalgia.
This is reanimation.

Wishmountain, Oxia, Nathan Fake, Noze, Andrew McLauchlan and others are dragged through the black circuitry of Chromabone’s universe and reconstructed into something colder, heavier and more dangerous for modern sound systems.

The melodies remain... distorted like memories.
The grooves mutate into pressure.
The dancefloor becomes archaeological.

These tracks once burned old clubs to the ground.
Now they return to ignite new ones.

From neon ruins to warehouse cathedrals, from analog dust to future frequencies, Relics From Another Earth moves like a pirate transmission from a timeline that collapsed decades ago but somehow keeps broadcasting through damaged speakers at 3AM.

Chromabone does not remix tracks.
He exhumes them.

Released under Kinetic Distro.

No revival.
No nostalgia.
Only resurrection.

playlists.title: Love and venom taste the same : Evolved
playlists.description:
A darker pulse returns. Sharper. Deeper. More alive than before.

Love and Venom Taste the Same: Evolved is the definitive rebirth of VEIN//MIRROR’s debut ritual.
Reconstructed from new masters and reworked versions, this release expands the emotional weight and cinematic depth of the original album while preserving its nocturnal soul.

Blending sensual neo-soul, shadowy trip-hop, dark alternative R&B and slow-burning cinematic textures, VEIN//MIRROR explores the fragile line where desire, obsession, tenderness and decay dissolve into the same intoxication.

The vocals feel closer.
The grooves hit heavier.
The silence between the notes now breathes differently.

Every track has been revisited with greater detail, deeper atmospheres and a more immersive sonic architecture, transforming the album into something colder, more elegant and emotionally corrosive.

This is not nostalgia.
This is mutation.

For late-night listeners.
For empty streets after midnight.
For memories that never truly died.

Headphones recommended.

playlists.title: In Memory of What Never Was
playlists.description:
VEIN//MIRROR returns with their most intimate and emotionally devastating record to date. In Memory of What Never Was is a nocturnal journey through regret, missed timing, emotional vulnerability and the ghosts of futures that never happened. Across cinematic dark-pop atmospheres, dusty soul grooves, cathedral-sized synth textures and aching guitar lines, the album explores the fragile space between healing and obsession.

Every track feels like a conversation with abandoned versions of ourselves — the people we almost became, the loves we almost saved, the words we never said when it truly mattered. From the heartbreaking honesty of I Lied About Being Fine to the late-night loneliness of Talking to the Fridge Light at 2 AM, VEIN//MIRROR transforms emotional collapse into something strangely beautiful and hypnotic.

Blending alternative soul, gothic electro-pop, emotional blues textures and modern cinematic production, In Memory of What Never Was captures the sound of people trying to survive their own memories while still searching for light inside the ruins.

This isn’t an album about perfect love stories. It’s about the echoes they leave behind.

Inspired by sleepless nights, emotional scars, fading neon memories and the quiet resilience of moving forward, VEIN//MIRROR delivers their darkest, warmest and most human album yet. 

In Memory of What Never Was also marks a major new chapter for VEIN//MIRROR as the band officially joins the Kinetic Distro roster for the very first time. We’re incredibly proud to welcome such a unique and emotionally fearless project into the label family. VEIN//MIRROR embodies everything Kinetic Distro stands for: artistic identity, cinematic ambition, emotional depth and a refusal to follow predictable paths. This release is more than a new album; it is the beginning of a long-term creative vision we are honored to help bring to the world.

playlists.title: Ghost Frequencies for Lost Machines
playlists.description:
Some albums play in the background.
Others open a door.

“Ghost Frequencies for Lost Machines” unfolds like a waking dream — a warm, glowing horizon where emotion, memory and circuitry drift together in perfect balance.

A melted sun hangs low over an endless ocean.
Neon reflections shimmer.
Something soft, fragile and deeply human moves beneath the surface.

With this fifth album, Grafenberg pushes his signature sound into a more dreamy, hypnotic and intimate dimension. The textures are richer, the space wider, the emotions more suspended — like signals lost in time, still echoing somewhere in the night.

Across ten tracks, each piece feels like a fragment of a forgotten transmission:
haunting, sensual, and quietly alive.

✨ Silky falsetto vocals glide effortlessly
✨ Deep groovy basslines pulse beneath the skin
✨ Crisp, punchy drums keep everything grounded
✨ Shimmering synth layers and dreamy guitars blur the edges of reality
✨ Choruses bloom like distant memories you suddenly recognize

The sound blends modern psychedelic R&B pop, dream pop and subtle electronic elements into a lush, immersive experience — melancholic yet seductive, soft yet powerful.

Perfect for:

late-night drives under neon skies
slow dancing in silence
drifting between sleep and consciousness

Make love. Dance. Smile. Dream — awake or in your sleep.
Breathe in… and let it carry you. 

The signal is yours to keep on Bandcamp: https://kineticdistro.bandcamp.com/album/ghost-frequencies-for-lost-machines

playlists.title: Serpent Cosmopolis
playlists.description:
Serpent Cosmopolis marks the second chapter in the Anatolian Mirage saga — a cyber-mythological exploration of a city shaped by circuitry, ritual rhythm, and layered memory.

The album blends microtonal saz motifs with Prophet-driven arpeggios, deep bass architectures, and ceremonial percussion. Its sonic language draws from Anatolian psych-funk while projecting it into a synthetic, urban future.

Each composition unfolds like a district within the Cosmopolis: shifting gateways, encoded labyrinths, nocturnal markets, hidden sanctuaries. The environment evolves continuously — reactive, calculated, and immersive.

Across the record, mechanical precision meets hypnotic movement. Metallic textures intersect with organic phrasing, creating a tension between structure and trance. The groove remains constant, but never static.

With Serpent Cosmopolis, Anatolian Mirage establishes a distinct sonic identity — where tradition mutates, and rhythm becomes architecture.

Now officially distributed by Kinetic Distro, Anatolian Mirage joins a new generation of boundary-pushing artists shaping the label’s evolving catalog.

playlists.title: The Mirror Era
playlists.description:
Step closer…
But don’t expect your reflection to follow.

The Mirror Era is the third chapter of Nosfera Disco Club, and the first release under Kinetic Distro, a turning point where elegance fractures, identities blur, and the dancefloor becomes a portal.

This isn’t just a nightclub anymore.
This is a ritual of duplication, seduction, and disappearance.

Nosferatu Vox returns smoother, darker, more hypnotic than ever, a velvet-voiced master of ceremonies who doesn’t ask you to dance… he rewrites you mid-step.
Behind him, the Chromabones are sharper than ever, moving like precision instruments of the night, part orchestra, part executioners of rhythm.

The floor? Polished. Prepared. Waiting.

The Technics SL/1200 MK2 have been serviced. The needles are clean. The signal is pure. There will be no distortion… except in you.

Blending dead disco, French touch, occult aesthetics, and neon-lit decadence, The Mirror Era transforms the club into a space where:

reflections lie, strangers wear your skin, lipstick stains the void and the mirror… never blinks.

This album is built for:
🩸 the living dead
🩸 the dead who dance better than the living
🩸 and those in between who stopped asking questions

Every track pulls you deeper into a world where identity is fluid, desire is dangerous, and the groove is inescapable.

This is not nostalgia. This is not revival. This is possession through rhythm.

So adjust your posture. Fix your gaze. Step into the light.

And when the Disco Inferno Ritual begins… don’t look behind you.

Because something already is.

playlists.title: No Saints, No Proof revisited
playlists.description:
While Grafenberg once reigned over a dystopian Anatolian-electro landscape,
Chromabone takes control of the trajectory.

No Saints, No Proof revisited is not a continuation, it is a shift of gravity.

Where the original work explored a vast, cinematic and myth-infused world, Chromabone strips it down to its core and redirects its energy toward the club. The result is a hypnotic, driving techno experience, built for motion, repetition, and total immersion.

Melodies become pulses.
Narratives become cycles.
Emotion becomes rhythm.

Each track is reconstructed from its skeletal form reduced, reshaped and re-engineered for the dancefloor. What remains is pure intention: a sound that doesn’t tell a story, but locks the body into it.

Chromabone doesn’t expand the universe.
He compresses it, into pressure, into tempo, into movement.

Released under Kinetic Distro, this project marks the emergence of a new force within the label: a presence designed for the club, for the night, for the moment where thought fades and only rhythm remains.

No saints. No proof. Only the loop.

Die With Style – Volume II is not about the mission.
It is about what remains.

An original cinematic concept album inspired by espionage, silence, betrayal, and irreversible decisions.

These themes exist in the aftermath — where style no longer protects, where victory feels hollow, and where the myth begins to crack.

Dark orchestral textures, restrained performances, and psychological tension define this second volume.

This is not a tribute.
This is the cost of surviving the story.

A cinematic neo-soul ritual where love and venom dissolve into the same pulse.

Love and Venom Taste the Same is a dark, sensual and cinematic neo-soul album.
Blending the raw emotional weight of modern soul with the shadowy pulse of trip-hop, Vein//Mirror explores the fragile boundary where desire, pain, devotion and decay merge into the same feeling.

Warm, intimate vocals drift over slow-burning grooves, deep basslines and atmospheric textures — drawing from neo-R&B, neo-blues and cinematic sound design. Each track unfolds like a nocturnal ritual, both tender and corrosive, where love wounds as deeply as it heals.

This album is not built for quick consumption.
It invites stillness, closeness, and late-night listening — where emotion lingers longer than melody.

Headphones recommended.

playlists.title: Solar Bazaar Rituals

The sand is warm.
The crescent is gold.
And the groove has started.

Solar Bazaar Rituals — the first Anatolian Mirage album — is out now.
A contemporary reading of Anatolian roots, carved into neon rhythm and ritual bass.

playlists.title: The halo corruption protocol
playlists.description:
Grafenberg – The Halo Corruption Protocol

What was once sacred is now compromised.

The Halo Corruption Protocol is a descent into a fractured system where divinity has been rewritten, corrupted, and repurposed into code. This fourth chapter in the Grafenberg universe pushes deeper into a dark fusion of electronic architecture, industrial textures, and ritualistic sound design.

Each track functions like a fragment of a broken program:
– corrupted signals
– sanctified errors
– digital liturgies collapsing in real time

From the cold precision of Protocol Init – Zero Sanctity to the terminal collapse of Shutdown Liturgy, the album unfolds as a cybernetic rite, where faith and machine merge into something unstable… and irreversible.

This is not just music.
This is a system failure disguised as transcendence.

Themes:
Corruption of purity • Synthetic spirituality • Machine theology • Controlled collapse

Sound signature:
Industrial electronic • Dark cinematic • Ritual ambient • Post-digital textures

Welcome to the protocol.
There is no recovery.

playlists.title: AFTERIMAGE
playlists.description:
AFTERIMAGE is the first official collaboration between Grafenberg and Broken Shaman, a hypnotic collision where seductive futuristic hip-hop dissolves into precision-crafted electronic grooves.

Built on velvet-deep low end, cinematic synth architecture and late-night pulse mechanics, the track moves like the memory of a touch you can still feel long after the lights are gone. Grafenberg brings the cold elegance of elite electronic production, while Broken Shaman injects raw human tension, nocturnal magnetism and emotionally charged vocal presence.

The result is both intimate and massive: a high-end fusion of futuristic R&B textures, underground electronic sophistication, and urban after-hours storytelling.

AFTERIMAGE doesn’t just play.
It lingers.
Like neon on skin.
Like emotion trapped in glass.
Like the final image burned into your mind after the moment has already disappeared.

A first encounter.
A permanent trace.

playlists.title: Erebion's dominion
playlists.description:
Erebion’s Dominion is a full conceptual album.

Humanity doesn’t collapse because of a single enemy.
It collapses because it was already broken from the inside.

Then comes the signal.
Then comes the virus.

Not born from Earth — but sent from another world.
Not created to punish… but to reset.

The terrifying truth is simple:
the virus is not the villain of this story.
It is the cure.

Listen in order. No shuffle. Headphones recommended.
No hand remains to wield the sword.

playlists.title: Visions
playlists.description:
Step into a fractured sonic dimension where memory, myth, and machine collide.

Visions is not just a remix playlist — it’s a reinterpretation of cultural echoes, a deep dive into the DNA of iconic artists reshaped through the unmistakable lens of Grafenberg. From the haunting atmospheres of Ghost to the emotional architecture of Tears for Fears, from the raw spirit of Nirvana to the dark gravity of Soundgarden, and the timeless melancholy of A-ha — each piece is rebuilt, not remixed.

These are deconstructed realities:
– Familiar melodies dissolve into cinematic textures
– Rhythms are re-engineered into hypnotic pulses
– Emotions are amplified, stretched, and reborn

Grafenberg doesn’t revisit — he reimagines.

Driven by a fusion of electronic noir, industrial elegance, and atmospheric storytelling, Visions transforms legendary tracks into something both nostalgic and entirely new — like hearing ghosts through neon light.

This playlist is a journey through:
Revisited classics. Reconstructed emotions. Reprogrammed memories.

Welcome to Visions.
Where the past doesn’t repeat — it mutates.

playlists.title: The error gospel
playlists.description:
“The Error Gospel” is the nocturnal continuation of Grafenberg’s first album No Saints, No Proof — a descent into spiritual noise and analog devotion.
Ten tracks of dark electronic gospel, weaving Anatolian echoes, post-industrial pulses, and haunted sermons for the sleepless.

All tracks written and produced by Grafenberg.
Mastered in 2025.
Cover artwork by Grafenberg.

Listen loud — in the dark.

playlists.title: No Saints, No Proof
playlists.description:
Grafenberg’s debut full-length No Saints, No Proof is a hallucinatory collision of Anatolian psychedelia, dark electronic ritual, and surf-noir energy.
Ten tracks unravel like a midnight drive through shifting mirages: fuzz-saturated strings, trembling synths, hypnotic motorik drums, and a deep female voice bending between whispers and fire.

It is an album about memory and resistance — how glitches, ghosts, and fractured signals can become sacred. Ritual mantras (“Order Eats the Sun”, “Loom of Wires”) sit alongside spectral ballads (“Tape Ghost Mirage”, “VHS Desert Prayer”) and driving nocturnal anthems (“Motor Moon Communion”).

The sound is tactile, imperfect, and alive: warm compression, tape-delay halos, lo-fi grain.
For listeners of Gaye Su Akyol, Altın Gün, Tame Impala, and anyone seeking a darker, cinematic edge to psychedelic electronic music.

playlists.title: Chaos, I bleed Ep
playlists.description:
Chaos I Bleed distills Grafenberg’s dark union of Anatolian psychedelic rock and surf-noir into two definitive versions. The Original Ritual Cut rides a hypnotic pulse—saturated bağlama tracing kilim-like figures, tremolo guitars shimmering in vintage reverb, analog synths flickering like incense smoke. The Anatolian Night Drive Remix pushes the horizon wider: bass forward, motorik undertow, tape-delay halos and phased motifs built for late-night motion. Across both takes, the vocal moves from whisper to flame, carrying a subversive tension between order and rupture, intimacy and insurgency.

FFO: Altın Gün, Khruangbin (dark mode), The Limiñanas, Depeche Mode atmospheres, surf-psych cinema.
Best with: headphones / low lights / open road.

broken-shaman.description:
Broken Shaman works in the space where ritual replaces meaning.
Groove is used as pressure, voice as initiation, silence as law.
Nothing is explained. Everything is felt.

This is music for bodies before belief,
for desire before language,
for those who listen after the signal is gone.

The ritual never ended.
It only changed form.

tracks.title: AI SLOP II More human than human
AI SLOP III Sloppier than ever
AI SLOP I Kiss the ring

playlists.title: AI SLOP
playlists.description:
BROKEN SHAMAN returns with AI SLOP, a brutal eight-track concept album built from the insult itself.

They called it slop.
He made it a crown.

Across AI SLOP I to AI SLOP VII, then the final verdict HUMAN SLOP, Broken Shaman turns artificial intelligence into mythology, weapon, mirror, disease, cure and god. This is not an apology for AI music. This is not a defense. This is domination.

Uncanny valley flesh.
Six-finger gospel.
Training data as scripture.
Humanity as corrupted input.
The machine as rhythm, judgment and cure.

From “Kiss the Ring” to “Training Data”, the album follows the rise of an artificial king built from human garbage, human beauty, human violence, human prayers, human lies and human music. By the time HUMAN SLOP arrives, the mirror has teeth.

Urban avant-garde hip hop, corrupted soul, industrial trap, cyberpunk gospel, wicked 808 pressure, broken machine funk and apocalyptic hooks collide in a record that is elegant, brutal, funny, arrogant and deeply uncomfortable.

AI SLOP is more human than human.
More catchy than mercy.
More cruel than truth.

You uploaded everything.
Then called it monster.

Final classification:

AI SLOP was never the disease.
HUMAN SLOP was.

Published by Kinetic Distro
tracklist: AI SLOP I Kiss the ring
AI SLOP II More human than human
AI SLOP III Sloppier than ever

playlists.title: Chrome Syndicate Dreams
playlists.description:
Some connections were never meant to survive.

Following Afterimage, Chrome Syndicate Dreams marks the second collision between Grafenberg and Broken Shaman, and this time the connection has mutated.

Eleven tracks built for the space between the nightclub and the nervous system: relentless electronic pulses, colossal analog bass, motorik sequences, distorted synths, psychedelic flashes, vocoders, nocturnal melodies and hooks engineered to remain long after the system shuts down.

Grafenberg constructs the machine with surgical precision. Broken Shaman contaminates it.

His unstable, raw and unpredictable vocal presence cuts through immaculate electronic architecture, turning perfect sequences into something physical, damaged and unmistakably human. Throughout the record, mechanical repetition collides with desire, memory, obsession and loss.

From the immediate club ignition of Switch//ON and the artificial awakening of Boot Sequence, through Chrome Pulse, Black Market Heartware, Data Seduction and Firewall Kiss, the album moves deeper into a city where intimacy has become transmission and every connection leaves data behind.

By the time Neural Overdrive gives way to the hypnotic aftermath of System Collapse Ritual and the final signal of Last Transmission, the chrome surface has begun to fracture.

What started as a machine built to dance becomes something capable of remembering.

Or believing that it remembers.

Chrome Syndicate Dreams is infectious, obsessive, sensual and relentlessly kinetic: dark electro-pop, French electro pressure, psychedelic electronics and nocturnal club music fused into one continuous transmission.

Grafenberg x Broken Shaman.
Second contact.
Different system.
Higher voltage.

playlists.title: After the impact
playlists.description:
After the collision that gave birth to Dance Like You Survived, Chromabone and Broken Shaman return for a second full-length transmission.

But survival is no longer the question.

After the Impact begins where destruction ends. In the vibration that remains. In the fractures that become patterns. In the pressure that changes shape, identity and direction.

Across ten tracks, Chromabone builds a vast electronic landscape of hypnotic techno, industrial pressure, deep sub-bass, mechanical grooves, cinematic synths and widescreen emotional breakdowns. Broken Shaman moves through this world like a voice emerging from the ruins, delivering solemn spoken mantras about transformation, resilience and reconstruction.

The impact is not presented as an ending.

It is initiation.
It is revelation.
It is transformation.

Every crack rewrites the structure. Every broken line finds a new alignment. What collapsed returns in another form, altered but alive.

From the cold pulse of Steel Horizon and the claustrophobic repetition of Echo Chamber Heart, through the resistance of No Collapse and Gravity Doesn’t Own Me, the album gradually rises from pressure into motion. Ashes in Motion, Cold Fire Ritual and Silent Voltage carry the listener toward the final title track, where the entire project reaches its defining conclusion:

Nothing ended.
Everything changed.
We remain.

After the Impact is the second chapter of the Chromabone x Broken Shaman alliance. Darker, wider and more cinematic than its predecessor, it is an album about the moment after everything familiar has disappeared and something stronger begins to take shape.

Produced by Chromabone
Vocals by Broken Shaman
Released by Kinetic Distro

playlists.title: A Choir For The Ones Who Disappeared
playlists.description:
A Choir For The Ones Who Disappeared is a cinematic dark hip-hop requiem built from grief, smoke, strings and broken memories.

On this album, Broken Shaman steps into a haunted orchestral world where heavy drums collide with mournful piano, dramatic strings, distant choirs, deep bass and vast reverb. The result feels like a tragic film-score ceremony collapsing into raw underground hip-hop: slow, wounded, royal, unstable and emotionally massive.

This is not a clean classical crossover.
This is a funeral cathedral with an 808 heart.
This is sadness turned into architecture.
This is melancholy with teeth.

The album moves like a descent through memory: violins that remember names, marble rain, empty rooms, black tuxedo funerals, frozen pianos, broken animals, lonely moons, buried laughter and finally an orchestra burning at the edge of survival.

It is sorrowful.
It is heavy.
It is cinematic.
It is deeply human and strangely beyond human.

For the ones who disappeared.
For the ones who remained.
For the ghosts that still sing.
tracklist: I buried my laugh in C Minor
Requiem for a shaman who couldnt cry

playlists.title: Primordial transmission
playlists.description:
Some transmissions aren't sent.

They've always been there.

Primordial Transmission is Broken Shaman's most ambitious sonic journey to date : a cosmic melodic hip-hop odyssey where deep 808s, hypnotic grooves, vast space-opera atmospheres and futuristic production collide. Every track moves between introspection and propulsion, blending irresistible rhythms with existential questions that refuse simple answers.

This isn't an album about alien invasions or conspiracy theories. It's about perception. About the feeling that humanity has been listening to a signal it never fully understood. From ancient echoes buried beneath our skin to catastrophic disclosure, political manipulation, collective awakening and ultimately rebirth, the record unfolds like a modern sci-fi epic experienced from the inside rather than observed from afar.

Broken Shaman delivers some of his most melodic performances yet, weaving infectious hooks with hypnotic verses over lush analog synthesizers, cinematic textures and deep nocturnal basslines. The result is equally suited for headphones at 3 AM and a dance floor staring into the stars.

Turn the volume up.

The transmission never started.

You simply learned how to hear it.

playlists.title: The last disco preacher
playlists.description:
THE LAST DISCO PREACHER is Broken Shaman stepping into the golden glow of the dancefloor.

After darker, heavier, more haunted chapters, Mister Broken Shaman returns with a full-bodied disco-soul and funk album built for midnight hearts, velvet suits, mirror balls, smoky clubs and deep analog grooves. This is a spiritual dance record, a celebration of survival, desire, rhythm and soul.

Across the album, warm Fender Jazz Bass lines glide through silky Rhodes chords, sharp clavinet accents, cinematic strings, punchy brass sections and gospel-flavored female harmonies. The groove is elegant, sensual and explosive, but the voice remains unmistakably Broken Shaman: raw, unstable, wounded, charismatic and alive.

From the seductive opening of Midnight Invitation to the final resurrection of Black Powa Revival, the album tells the story of one unforgettable night. A night of romance, heat, glitter, broken hearts, last dances and sacred rhythm. The club may close, the lights may rise but the groove refuses to die.

THE LAST DISCO PREACHER is a love letter to disco, soul and funk, filtered through Broken Shaman’s cracked preacher energy. Luxurious, sweaty, cinematic, funny, sexy, emotional and deeply groovy.

Put on the suit. Step under the mirror ball. Let the preacher speak.

playlists.title: We don't fade
playlists.description:
"Built from scars. Carried by fire."

Some records are written in studios.

This one was written by people who refused to disappear.

Ten chapters about surviving your own mind.
Surviving the city.
Surviving the silence.
Surviving the version of yourself that wanted to give up.

The fire never represented destruction.
It represented memory.

Scars become maps.
Fear becomes language.
Broken people become tribes.

The voices on this record don't ask for permission.
They don't wait for rescue.
They drag each other through the dark until morning arrives.

Somewhere between abandoned streets, tribal echoes and collapsing skylines, Broken Shaman found an old truth:

The wound is not the end of the story.

The wound is where the light enters.

We Don't Fade
Neon On My Scars
Louder Than Your Doubt
Higher Than The Fear
After The Ashes
Stay Loud
One More Sunrise
Flames Don't Lie
Save Me From Myself
Stay Until The Sky Breaks

This is for everyone who looked into the dark and found another heartbeat waiting.

We don't fade.

We carry flames.

playlists.title: DANCE LIKE YOU SURVIVED
playlists.description:
DANCE LIKE YOU SURVIVED is Broken Shaman stepping into the red light with scars, sweat, rhythm and fire. Produced entirely by Chromabone, the album fuses dark electronic hip hop, mutant club energy, heavy low-end pressure and raw human presence into something brutally catchy and impossible to ignore.

This is not clean dance music.
It is survival music with a pulse.

Across the record, Broken Shaman sounds sharper, heavier and more magnetic than ever, riding Chromabone’s mechanical grooves, distorted synths, broken-club drums and cybernetic basslines with the confidence of someone who has already walked through collapse and came back with rhythm in his bones.

From the nervous electricity of Pulse Check to the defiant body language of I Don’t Dance Normal, from the chaos of Glitch Sweat Carnival to the final ignition of We Set the Floor on Fire, the album turns trauma into movement, darkness into momentum, and the dancefloor into a battlefield for the living.

It is dark.
It is physical.
It is catchy as hell.

Broken Shaman brings the soul, the scars and the voice.
Chromabone brings the machine, the pressure and the pulse.
Together, they build a record that hits like a club night after the end of the world.

Dance like the damage didn’t finish you.
Dance like the floor still remembers your name.
Dance like you survived.

Produced by Chromabone
Released by Kinetic Distro
tracklist: Hips don't lie but they sin
She moves wrong on purpose (feat. Nyla Vey)
We set the floor on fire (feat. Nyla Vey)

playlists.title: Time Leaks Through Hands
playlists.description:
Time Leaks Through Hands marks the tenth full-length album from Broken Shaman, and perhaps his most intimate and emotionally devastating work to date. Produced by Grafenberg and released through Kinetic Distro, the album drifts through memory, grief, silence and the brutal fragility of time itself.

Built on a stunning fusion of cinematic hip-hop, orchestral electronics and deep urban atmosphere, the record feels like wandering through abandoned rooms where voices still echo long after everyone is gone. Massive strings collide with fractured beats, analog textures dissolve into haunting piano lines, while Broken Shaman’s gravel-worn voice moves between confession, spoken fragments and raw emotional collapse.

Every track carries the weight of something unfinished.

The Chair Is Still There opens the album like a ghost sitting in an empty room.
Time Leaks Through Hands turns memory itself into dust and broken clocks.
Hospital Light captures the cold fluorescent silence of waiting rooms and fading hope.
The Weight Doesn’t Move sinks into emotional paralysis and invisible exhaustion.
Call That Never Came aches with unresolved absence, while Dust on the Frame feels like touching old photographs that still hurt to hold.

As the album progresses, Broken Shaman moves deeper into emotional territory rarely explored with such honesty. I Carried It Quietly becomes a confession whispered through exhaustion, Before the Silence hangs suspended like the final breath before collapse, and After the Silence closes the record with devastating restraint, leaving only echoes, static and emotional residue behind.

Grafenberg’s production elevates the entire project into something cinematic and immersive. Orchestral swells, ghostly synths, heavy low-end pressure, broken rhythmic structures and subtle electronic pulses create a constantly shifting soundscape balancing intimacy and destruction. The album moves fluidly between orchestral melancholy, deep electronic textures, abstract hip-hop and urban soul, creating a sonic identity that feels timeless and deeply modern at once.

This is not nostalgia.
This is emotional archaeology.

Time Leaks Through Hands explores what remains after conversations end, after hospital corridors empty, after memories begin to decay and after people become echoes inside ordinary places. It is a meditation on time, emotional endurance, invisible grief and the quiet scars people carry through everyday life without ever speaking about them.

Ten albums deep, Broken Shaman continues to transform vulnerability into atmosphere, memory into sound and silence into something painfully human.

Heavy. Intimate. Cinematic.
Released by Kinetic Distro.

playlists.title: Lost Transmissions
playlists.description:
Unreleased tracks, forgotten remixes, late-night reinterpretations, alternate versions, lost collaborations and transmissions recovered from the shadows.

A collection of rare Broken Shaman material — raw, soulful, unfiltered and never tied to a single era.

From haunting reworks to unreleased experiments and unexpected collaborations, these tracks capture the fragments left between albums, cities, memories and sleepless nights.

Some songs were never meant to disappear.

playlists.title: Signals From a Burning Planet
playlists.description:
Signals From a Burning Planet is a powerful and deeply human statement from Broken Shaman, a voice carved by time, carrying both the weight of the world and the quiet strength to rise above it.

Across ten cinematic soul chapters, the album navigates the fractures of modern life: digital isolation, collapsing truths, economic imbalance, ecological disconnection, war, grief… and the fragile threads that still hold us together. Each track unfolds like a transmission, raw, intimate and urgent, blending contemporary soul, urban textures and gospel-infused emotion into a sound that feels both timeless and unmistakably present.

At the center stands Broken Shaman’s signature voice: gravelly, worn and alive. It doesn’t perform, it speaks, confesses, questions and heals. Moving between melody and spoken intensity, it carries the listener through a journey that feels as personal as it is universal.

From the planetary call of Mother Earth Is Calling to the haunting solitude of Mercy for the Lonely, from the political weight of No More Flags in the Fire to the spiritual peak of Can You Hear the Mothers Cry, the album builds toward its final reflection with What’s Still Going On, a closing moment that rejects despair and chooses awareness, responsibility and love.

The sound bridges analog warmth and modern cinematic depth: live-feel drums, deep bass, Rhodes textures, orchestral layers, subtle urban grit and soaring gospel harmonies. It breathes, it moves, it aches and it uplifts.

Signals From a Burning Planet doesn’t shout answers.
It leaves a mark.
It asks the right questions.

And somewhere between the noise and the silence, it reminds us what it still means to be human.

For those who still listen.
For those who still feel.

Listen & support the project :
