playlists.title: Cold Calculus
playlists.description:
Step into the world of Broken Shaman with “Cold Calculus,” an album where raw urban life is viewed through the precise, often brutal lens of a chessboard. This soul/hip-hop fusion blends powerful, slice-of-life narratives with a pervasive metaphor: the world as a 64-square grid where every decision is a calculation and every consequence is inescapable.

Broken Shaman’s poetic, often vulnerable flow is balanced against complex, structured production, creating a unique sonic tension between human emotion and cold logic. It’s a powerful, introspective journey into the flaws of existence, the fragility of strategy, and the ultimate realization that the game’s greatest opponent is often yourself.

playlists.title: AFTERIMAGE
playlists.description:
AFTERIMAGE is the first official collaboration between Grafenberg and Broken Shaman, a hypnotic collision where seductive futuristic hip-hop dissolves into precision-crafted electronic grooves.

Built on velvet-deep low end, cinematic synth architecture and late-night pulse mechanics, the track moves like the memory of a touch you can still feel long after the lights are gone. Grafenberg brings the cold elegance of elite electronic production, while Broken Shaman injects raw human tension, nocturnal magnetism and emotionally charged vocal presence.

The result is both intimate and massive: a high-end fusion of futuristic R&B textures, underground electronic sophistication, and urban after-hours storytelling.

AFTERIMAGE doesn’t just play.
It lingers.
Like neon on skin.
Like emotion trapped in glass.
Like the final image burned into your mind after the moment has already disappeared.

A first encounter.
A permanent trace.

playlists.title: Velvet Predator
playlists.description:
Velvet Predator doesn’t chase. It waits.

This album lives in the dark, in low light, slow breath, controlled tension.
Every track moves like a body that already knows what it wants.

From After Midnight Instructions to Stay Until the Morning Breaks,
this is a ritual of presence, dominance and silence.

Nothing is rushed.
Nothing is loud.
Everything is intentional.

The bass doesn’t hit, it pulls.
The groove doesn’t drop, it wraps.
The voice doesn’t shout, it gets closer.

This is not about love.
Not about chaos.
Not even about desire.

It’s about control.

A game played without witnesses.
A tension built without release.
A connection that happens before words exist.

Velvet Predator is movement in the dark.
Breath against skin.
Stillness that says everything.

Turn off the lights.
You’ll understand.

playlists.title: No armor
playlists.description:
“No Armor” is the most intimate Broken Shaman record to date.

No mythology.
No ritual mask.
No armor.

Just memory.

Built on dusty boom bap textures, warm Rhodes chords and fragile late-night verses, this album explores the quiet spaces where grief actually lives, not in explosions of pain, but in the slow erosion of ordinary days.

Kitchen tables.
Hospital hallways.
Last voicemails.
Empty Sundays.

Across eleven minimal, analog-feeling tracks, Broken Shaman strips everything down to the essentials: close-mic confessions, loose swing drums, upright bass lines and the soft hiss of vinyl.

The beats breathe.
The silence matters.
Nothing is hidden.

“No Armor” is about loss that doesn’t shout.
The kind that sits quietly across the table.

And waits.

If previous Broken Shaman records were rituals, this one is a conversation.

playlists.title: Iron Monk Execution
playlists.description:
Ten tracks built like a training cycle : discipline, repetition, isolation, precision. 
There are no wasted movements here. No emotional overflow, no theatrical chaos.
Every beat is measured.
Every bassline restrained.
Every lyric delivered like a blade that already knows where it will land.

Steel logic.
Breath before strike.

Iron Monk Execution is what happens when emotion is forged into weaponry.

playlists.title: You were born ready
playlists.description:
YOU WERE BORN READY

This is not music.
This is temptation made audible.

"You Were Born Ready" is the sound of surrender before the fall. The moment between restraint and ruin. The instant your body understands before your mind agrees.

Every track breathes heat. Slow, deliberate pressure. Analog bass that moves like skin against skin. Voices that don’t ask — they decide.

She is always there. Not chasing. Not forcing. Waiting.

A presence in the dark. A whisper behind your ear. A hand hovering just close enough to erase resistance.

This album lives in that space where control dissolves. Where desire becomes gravity. Where you stop asking why and start accepting what was always inevitable.

It is sacred.
It is predatory.
It is intimate.
It is merciless.

This is the forbidden fruit already in your hand.

You were not convinced.

You were recognized.

You were born ready.

playlists.title: After the feed
playlists.description:
After the Feed is what happens when the signal dies… but the body keeps moving.

No more outrage cycles.
No more trending panic.
No more narrative to cling to.

Just reflex. Memory. Residual input.

This album explores the space after collapse — where systems fail quietly, machines keep praying without masters, and hands remember what language forgets. It’s not revolution. It’s decompression. It’s the slow recalibration of a nervous system that lived too long inside noise.

No hooks designed to save you.
No slogans left to repeat.
Only breath.
Only pulse.
Only the long silence after transmission.

This is survival without spectacle.

playlists.title: Fire & Ice
playlists.description:
Born from surveillance, obedience, collapse, and silence, this record documents a world freezing in control while burning in denial. Power speaks softly. Violence moves quietly. The machine keeps running even when no one believes in it anymore.

There are no heroes here. No slogans. No comfort.

Only pressure, cold systems, warm blood, and the moment where compliance cracks.

This is political music without speeches. Protest without flags. A soundtrack for the space between fear and revolt.

playlists.title: Dirt Temple
playlists.description:
Built on heavy low frequencies, feral grooves, and stripped-down incantations, Dirt Temple explores what remains when meaning collapses and instinct takes control.
There are no gods here—only breath, pressure, dirt, and repetition.

Each track functions like a descent: slower, heavier, more physical.
This is music made for the body before the mind, for movement before belief.

Enter quietly.
Nothing inside is clean.

anatolian-mirage.description:
From Istanbul’s shadows to digital temples,
Anatolian Mirage bends time through microtonal groove.
Ancient myths. Modern voltage. Endless coil.

playlists.title: Microtonic oasis collapse
playlists.description:
Microtonic Oasis Collapse is the fourth chapter in the evolving mythology of Anatolian Mirage — a desert hallucination where sacred geometry, collapsing mirages, impossible rhythms, and burning solar memory converge.

Built around fractured odd meters, microtonal saz spirals, prophet synth mirages, ritual percussion, and polymetric bass architecture, the album transforms the desert into a living intelligence. Ancient temples breathe in 7/8, sandstorms mutate in 19/8, halays become hallucinations, and collapsing golden oases reveal hidden dimensions beyond time.

Each track acts as a shifting zone within the mythic wasteland: ritual ruins, fractal temples, violent salt storms, dimensional caravans, and sacred deserts that calculate their own destruction.

Microtonic Oasis Collapse is the sound of rhythm surviving after reality fractures into sand.

playlists.title: Velvet sun empire
playlists.description:
Velvet Sun Empire is the third chapter in the Anatolian Mirage saga, a luminous but dangerous empire where ritual power, mythic architecture and hypnotic groove merge beneath an endless burning sun.

Built on deep analog basslines, microtonal saz melodies, prophetic synth arpeggios and ceremonial percussion, the album expands the sonic mythology of Anatolian Mirage into a grand imperial landscape. Ancient serpents, monolithic palaces, mirrored ballrooms, and sacred processions form a world where beauty and power exist in fragile balance.

Each track unveils a new domain of the Velvet Empire: mechanical thrones, glass prophets, golden parades, silent temples and collapsing kingdoms. The atmosphere moves between seductive warmth and quiet tension, where every rhythm feels like a ritual and every melody carries the echo of forgotten dynasties.

Velvet Sun Empire is a civilization built on rhythm, myth, and burning light.
tracklist: The Serpent Who Learned to Pray

iron-covenant.description:
“The Big Four were never four.”

Forged on the industrial East Coast, somewhere between rusted docks and dim basement clubs, Iron Covenant emerged in the early 80s with a paradoxical identity:
East Coast attitude. West Coast precision.

While Anthrax was shaking New York and the Californian scene was defining thrash metal’s future, Iron Covenant quietly carved its own path — blending surgical riff discipline, relentless rhythmic force, and unforgettable hooks.

Too technical to be just another thrash band.
Too raw and uncompromising to become mainstream.

They never chased the crown.
Eventually, it found them.

🧬 The Core Line-up

Jack “Razor” Haldane – vocals / rhythm guitar
Charismatic frontman with a voice balancing grit and melody.

Ethan Cross – lead guitar
Riff architect and obsessive craftsman of structure and detail.

Marko Vega – bass
Dark groove foundation, occasionally hinting at blues and funk influences.

Caleb North – drums
Precision machine. Metronomic power with surgical timing.

Remarkably, the band maintained nearly the same line-up for over three decades, a rare stability that helped shape its unmistakable sound.

playlists.title: Black Discipline
playlists.description:
“Perfection is the death of impulse.”

Released in 1989, Black Discipline stands as Iron Covenant’s most severe, mechanized, and conceptually focused record.

After the monumental architecture of Cathedrals of Noise (1986), the band deliberately stripped away atmosphere, grandeur, and progressive expansion to pursue something far more unsettling:

discipline as sound
control as structure
 efficiency as violence

This is the sound of a system correcting itself.

THE CONCEPT

Every track follows a logical descent into total control:

Rule
Deviation
Correction
Normalization
Optimization
Residual identity
Eradication
Final closure

The album moves like an ideological machine, where every riff functions as a command and every silence feels deliberate.

This is Iron Covenant at its most clinical, dry, and uncompromising.

THE SOUND

Compared to previous albums, Black Discipline introduces:

drier guitar tones
repetitive, system-like riff cycles
mechanical drum precision
reduced melodic release
severe dynamic control
oppressive low-mid punch
minimal atmosphere
groove as enforcement

The result is a record that feels less like performance and more like procedural execution.

TRACK ARC
“Black Discipline” — rule imposed
“System Drift” — silent deviation
“Corrective Force” — violence as solution
“Normalized State” — order restored
“Efficient Patterns” — discipline becomes seductive
“Residual Self” — human trace detected
“Zero Tolerance” — absolute eradication
“Closed Circuit” — system completion
Bonus: “After Function” — the trace that should not remain

LEGACY

Often cited by later groove-thrash, industrial metal, and extreme progressive acts, Black Discipline is widely regarded as one of Iron Covenant’s most radically coherent releases.

Not their most emotional.
Not their most accessible.
But arguably their most perfectly executed concept.

This is where the band replaced instinct with method.

playlists.title: Cathedrals of Noise
playlists.description:
“Structure became sound. Sound became control.”

By 1986, Iron Covenant had outgrown the limits of traditional thrash metal.

With Cathedrals of Noise, the band didn’t just evolve —
they redefined their own language.

This third album marks a decisive shift:

From speed to structure
From aggression to architecture
From instinct to intention

The riffs no longer just drive the songs, they build them.

A CONCEPT OF CONTROL

Cathedrals of Noise explores the idea of sound as a system :

Noise as structure
Structure as belief
Belief as control

Each track functions like a pillar within a larger design, forming an immersive and sometimes oppressive sonic environment.

This is not an album of singles. It is an experience.

MUSICAL EVOLUTION

Compared to previous releases, the album introduces :

- More progressive structures
- Slower, heavier sections contrasted with bursts of speed
- Complex, evolving riff patterns
- Greater dynamic range and tension
- A more atmospheric and cinematic approach

The band pushes beyond thrash conventions without abandoning its core intensity.

TRACK FLOW
“Cathedrals of Noise” — Sets the architecture, controlled and imposing
“Labyrinth Skin” — Twisting structures, shifting identity
“Grave Momentum” — Heavy, inevitable motion
“The Architecture of Faith” — Expansive, conceptual centerpiece
“Clear Through Fire” — Clarity emerging from chaos
“Break the Current” — Controlled release, forward momentum
“After the Spire” — Atmospheric descent, almost cinematic
“Rupture Doctrine” — Total collapse, explosive and final

 LEGACY
Initially misunderstood by part of the thrash audience, Cathedrals of Noise would later be recognized as:

- one of the earliest examples of progressive thrash metal with conceptual depth

- a record that proved heavy music could be both intellectual and physically powerful

This is where Iron Covenant stoppconcept album
ed being part of a movement…and became something else entirely.

playlists.title: Ashes & Wires
playlists.description:
After the raw urgency of their 1981 debut, Iron Covenant returned in 1983 with a record that didn’t just push forward, it deepened everything.

Ashes & Wires captures a band no longer discovering its sound, but refining its intent.

The speed is still there.
The aggression remains uncompromised.
But beneath it lies something new : control, contrast, emotional weight.

Where Forged in Concrete was instinct, Ashes & Wires is awareness.

playlists.title: Forged in concrete
playlists.description:
Raw. Fast. Immediate.

Recorded in just a few weeks with almost no production polish, Forged in Concrete captured a band operating on pure instinct and urgency.

Sharp riffs.
High tempo.
Chanted choruses built for sweat-filled rooms.

The sound is rough around the edges, but the hooks refuse to let go.


It’s an album that smells like steel, sweat, cheap beer and electricity, the sound of a band discovering its own power in real time.

nosfera-disco-club.description:
Dark disco for the undead.
We dance after midnight, after morals, after pulse checks.
Neon lights, velvet fangs, sticky floors.
Too funky to be dead. Too dead to be innocent.
Come dancing. Stay undead.

tracks.title: The last waltz of the damned

playlists.title: The ghouls of midnight
playlists.description:
Welcome back to the dancefloor…
Midnight has struck, the graves are open, and the party refuses to die.

The Ghouls of Midnight is the second album from Nosfera Disco Club, a darkly playful journey where spooky aesthetics meet irresistible disco grooves. Somewhere between neon-lit cemeteries and haunted nightclubs, skeletons, zombies and vampires gather to dance until dawn or beyond.

Blending dead disco, French-touch rhythms, and occult atmospheres, this album turns horror into celebration. Funky basslines crawl out of the grave, mechanical claps echo like bones on marble, and ghostly synths glow under a blood-red moon. It’s creepy, seductive, and unapologetically fun.

This is not music for fear, this is music for dancing with fear.

From hypnotic openers to full-blown undead anthems, The Ghouls of Midnight invites you into a world where every beat is cursed, every melody is possessed, and every track feels like a forbidden ritual disguised as a party.

Light a candle.
Raise the volume.
And don’t worry, the dead are friendly tonight.

playlists.title: Red veins on the dancefloor
playlists.description:
Red Veins on the Dancefloor is a nocturnal ritual.

A dark disco album born under neon lights and velvet shadows, where hypnotic basslines, ritual rhythms and cold synths pulse like blood through the club.

Each track moves between seduction and menace, glamour and decay — a dancefloor lit by chrome reflections, midnight desires and red-stained visions.

This is not nostalgia.
This is a modern vampire disco.
Welcome to Nosfera Disco Club.

vein-mirror.description:
VEIN//MIRROR is a dark, sensual and cinematic ritual of sound.
Born at the intersection of analog warmth and poetic violence, the project explores the fragile space where desire turns toxic and beauty becomes dangerous.

Driven by hypnotic rhythms, melancholic guitars, saturated Moog pulses, Mellotron choirs and deep, intimate vocals, VEIN//MIRROR creates immersive soundscapes that feel both ancient and futuristic. Each track unfolds like a fractured reflection — emotional, physical, and deeply immersive — where intimacy and brutality coexist.

Love and Venom Taste the Same, the debut album, is a journey through sensual decay, ritualistic tension and sacred collapse. A collection of cinematic scenes where love is never innocent, salvation is forged through sacrifice, and every breath carries the taste of poison.

VEIN//MIRROR is not a genre.
It is a ceremony, a wound, a mirror.
Music for those who seek the sacred in the forbidden — and the forbidden in the sacred.

playlists.title: Zero Cathedral
playlists.description:
Zero Cathedral is the fourth chapter in the evolving world of VEIN//MIRROR, a monumental descent into sacred architecture, cosmic silence and fractured light.

Built on cathedral-scale choirs, celestial guitar lines, deep sub-bass pulses and shimmering synth halos, the album explores the point where faith, collapse and transcendence become the same event. Every track feels like walking through the ruins of a divine structure that still remembers how to breathe.

Stone, stained glass, stars and echoes merge into a cinematic ritual where sorrow becomes illumination. Voices rise like prayers through abandoned halls, guitars bloom with sacred reverb, and every silence carries the weight of revelation.

Zero Cathedral is an album about the moment after the fall, when the ruins no longer symbolize loss, but transformation.
A place where the last light does not disappear.
It learns how to break.

playlists.title: Veins of Light, Veins of Rust
playlists.description:
Veins of Light, Veins of Rust explores the fragile tension between decay and illumination.

Where previous works drifted through silence and emotional resonance, this record moves closer to the body, to metal, to fracture, to transformation. Warm analog textures collide with corroded tones, shimmering guitars and slow-burning rhythms, creating a sound that feels both alive and deteriorating.

Each track unfolds like a process : something breaking down, something emerging. Rust becomes memory. Light becomes pressure. The voice moves through it all with quiet intensity, not resisting the collapse, but learning from it.

This is an album about change that cannot be reversed.
About beauty that exists because it fades.
About the strange glow that lives inside what is already falling apart.

playlists.title: The Hush Beneath The Static
playlists.description:
The Hush Beneath the Static is a slow descent into the space that remains after noise fades.

This album explores the tension between signal and silence, presence and absence, intimacy and distance. Built on warm analog textures, cinematic guitar lines, deep sub-bass and restrained electronic rhythms, VEIN//MIRROR crafts a sound that is contemplative, emotional and quietly powerful.

Each track unfolds like a suspended moment — breath held, pulse softened — where longing, memory and fragile connection drift beneath layers of static. The voice moves with restraint and vulnerability, guiding the listener through landscapes shaped by dusk, reflection and quiet transformation.

The Hush Beneath the Static is not about impact — it is about resonance.
Not collapse, but what survives after it.
A record made for late hours, empty spaces, and the subtle gravity of things left unspoken.

playlists.title: Slow burn dancing
playlists.description:
Slow Burn Dancing is the third album by Lykke, recorded in 1985.

More confident, sensual and rhythm-driven than its predecessors, the album moves through elegant disco textures, controlled emotion and late-night momentum.

Built on warm basslines, measured tempos and a refined balance between intimacy and distance, Slow Burn Dancing captures the group at its most poised and technically accomplished.

Beneath its polished surface, however, there is a quiet exhaustion — a sense of movement that never fully comes to rest.

An album about desire, control and the beauty of things that slowly begin to burn.

playlists.title: Shadows in motion
playlists.description:
Shadows in Motion is the second album by Lykke, recorded in 1981.

Where Northern Lights embraced clarity and warmth, this record moves inward — slower, darker and more deliberate.

Built around restrained arrangements, nocturnal atmospheres and a growing tension between stillness and movement, Shadows in Motion marks the beginning of Lykke’s artistic shift.

The melodies remain precise, but the spaces between them begin to matter just as much.

An album about distance, hesitation and the quiet weight of change.

playlists.title: Northern Lights
playlists.description:
Northern Lights is the debut album by Lykke, recorded in 1979.

Built around melodic songwriting and a delicate balance between female and male vocals, the album explores intimacy, waiting, and quiet emotional connection.

Blending elegant pop, subtle disco influences and a distinctly Nordic atmosphere, Northern Lights captures a moment of clarity and emotional warmth, before the band would later move toward darker and more introspective territory.

An album shaped by simplicity, restraint, and a fragile sense of happiness — the kind that exists just before silence.

Die With Style – Volume II is not about the mission.
It is about what remains.

An original cinematic concept album inspired by espionage, silence, betrayal, and irreversible decisions.

These themes exist in the aftermath — where style no longer protects, where victory feels hollow, and where the myth begins to crack.

Dark orchestral textures, restrained performances, and psychological tension define this second volume.

This is not a tribute.
This is the cost of surviving the story.

playlists.title: Songs for standing back up
playlists.description:
Songs for Standing Back Up is not about winning.
It’s about staying in the fight.

Ten cinematic rock songs inspired by the emotional DNA of classic 80s and 90s boxing films — not the glory, but the effort. Not the spotlight, but the sweat.

From the first bell to the final round, each track captures a different stage of resilience:
– doubt
– discipline
– pain
– vulnerability
– endurance
– dignity

Melodic guitar solos, analog warmth, male vocals with grit and honesty. No clichés. No victory speeches. Just the sound of someone choosing to stand back up — again and again.

This is a soundtrack for the underdog in all of us.

If you fall…
fall true.
Then stand back up.

playlists.title: Die with style
playlists.description:
Die With Style is an imaginary collection of original spy themes, a cinematic album inspired by the elegance, danger, and moral cost of espionage.

Each track plays like the theme of a film that never existed : love turning into betrayal, luxury masking violence, silence speaking louder than words, and victory leaving irreversible scars.

This is not a pastiche, nor a tribute album.
It is a parallel mythology, where orchestral tension, dark glamour, and emotional restraint meet modern cinematic storytelling.

Die With Style explores the space between legend and consequence, between impeccable tailoring and damaged souls.
These are themes for the spy we loved, not because he was flawless, but because he paid the price.

Volume I is the opening chapter.
